events.text: The night {npc} is born, every lamp in the street burns blue for an hour, and the river runs backwards past your door until the midwife finishes. Old people come out of their houses in their sleeping clothes. One of them, older than the rest, bows to the cradle.

choices.text: Ask the old one what it means

effects.log: "A child of a blessed house," the old one says. "Your world remembers who is good to it. Raise this one well."

choices.text: Close the shutters and hold the child

effects.log: You close the shutters on the blue light and hold {npc} until morning. Whatever the sign means, it can wait until breakfast.

choices.text: Thank the world out loud

effects.log: You stand in the doorway and thank the world, the river, the lamps. The neighbours pretend not to hear, and tell everyone.

events.text: In the morning after {npc} is born, a flock of white herons settles on your roof and will not leave. By noon half the town has come to look. By evening a messenger of the first kingdom is at your gate, asking politely whether the child has been promised to anyone.

choices.text: Say the child belongs to no one but the child

effects.log: The messenger writes that down very carefully, as if it were an answer to a much bigger question.

choices.text: Invite the messenger in for tea

effects.log: The messenger stays for tea, and for supper. The first kingdom will remember your house kindly.

events.text: {npc} is twelve, and the sign of the birth has not faded. Stray dogs follow {him} home. Wounded birds wait on the sill for {his} hands. And this spring {he} breathed in once by the river and the whole willow bent toward {him}.

choices.text: Teach {him} to hide it

effects.log: You teach {npc} to breathe small in a crowd. A blessed child is a target too.

choices.text: Teach {him} to use it

effects.log: You take {npc} out every morning to the willow. By autumn {he} breathes like a grown fighter.

choices.text: Let {him} be twelve

effects.log: You let {npc} be twelve: lazy, cheeky, late for supper. The blessing does not seem to mind.

events.text: A healer of {pw_people} comes a long way to see {npc}, now twelve, and asks to take {him} as an apprentice. "Children of a blessed house heal faster than any of us can teach," the healer says. "I would like to see how fast."

choices.text: Let {npc} decide

effects.log: {npc} decides at once, and goes for a summer, and comes home knowing the names of every herb on the hill.

choices.text: Say {npc} stays home

effects.log: The healer bows and leaves a book of herbs behind. {npc} reads it under the blanket every night.

events.text: Your master {npc} asks for a spar on the white jade terrace, as on a thousand mornings, with the cloud sea below. Today, at the hundredth exchange, {npc} steps back, lowers {his} hands, and smiles. Neither of you says it.

choices.text: Kneel and thank {npc} for every century of it

effects.log: You kneel on the jade. {npc} pulls you up by both hands. "Teach someone," {he} says. "That is how an immortal thanks a master."

choices.text: Bow as one immortal to another

effects.log: You bow, and {npc} returns it exactly, as to an equal. The cranes on the terrace roof watch the whole thing.

events.text: Your master {npc} has been sitting at the edge of your isle for a week, watching you train and saying nothing. On the eighth day {he} stands up, brushes the cloud-dew off {his} robe, and says: "I have nothing left to show you. That is the best thing a master can say."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay anyway

effects.log: {npc} stays a while longer, as a guest. You pour {his} tea now. It is strange, and good.

choices.text: Walk {npc} to the stairs

effects.log: You walk {npc} to the white stairs. At the top {he} turns, once, and you both laugh at nothing.

events.text: Your master {npc} comes to your domain and asks to see it, all of it, from end to end. At the far edge {he} stops and looks back at what you have made. "I could not have made this," {he} says. "You have gone past me."

choices.text: Give {npc} a place in your domain

effects.log: You give {npc} a hill in your domain, with a view of everything. {He} visits it more often than {he} admits.

choices.text: Bow as one god to another

effects.log: You bow, and {npc} returns it exactly. The worlds below feel a little steadier that day.

events.text: In a spar before the pantheon your master {npc} yields to you at the third exchange, and the gods watching go quiet. "Do not look at me like that," {npc} says afterwards. "I have been waiting for that for a thousand years."

choices.text: Ask {npc} what comes next

effects.log: "For me? Rest," {npc} says. "For you? Students. It never ends. That is the good part."

choices.text: Laugh with {npc}

effects.log: You laugh together until the pantheon begins to wonder what is funny. Nothing is, and everything.

events.text: The ferry bell, the smell of river weed, a woman on the far bank shaking out a red cloth. You are six, and the ferryman lets you pull the rope for the first time. On the third pull a heron lifts off the water so close you could touch it.

choices.text: Pull the rope as hard as you can

effects.log: The ferry lurches and everyone laughs, the ferryman loudest. You remember that laugh all your life.

choices.text: Watch the heron

effects.log: You watch the heron go up the river until it is a dot. Something in you goes with it.

events.text: This again. The ferry bell, the river weed, the red cloth on the far bank. You are six, and you know exactly when the heron will lift, and you have your hand out before it does.

choices.text: Pull the rope as hard as you can

effects.log: The ferry lurches and everyone laughs, the ferryman loudest. You remember that laugh all your life.

choices.text: Touch the heron this time

effects.log: Your fingertips brush its wing. It does not mind. The ferryman stares at you all the way across.

choices.text: Pull the rope for the ferryman, who is tired

effects.log: You pull it the whole way. Lives ago you never noticed how tired the ferryman was.

events.text: The first snow. You are six, and you wake to a white yard and a silence you have never heard. Someone of the house is already outside, laughing, with snow in their hair. A fox has walked across the yard in the night and left a line of prints to the gate.

choices.text: Run out barefoot

effects.log: Your feet sting for an hour and you do not care at all.

choices.text: Follow the fox prints

effects.log: They go to the gate and stop. You stand there a long time, wondering where a fox goes.

events.text: This again. The white yard, the silence, the laughing in the snow. You are six, and you know the fox's prints go to the gate and then to the old woodshed, where nobody has ever looked.

choices.text: Run out barefoot

effects.log: Your feet sting for an hour and you do not care at all.

choices.text: Look in the woodshed

effects.log: Behind the woodshed, in the snow, the fox has had her cubs. You are the only one who ever knows.

choices.text: Make the snow angel you always meant to

effects.log: You lie down in the snow and make one. Lives ago you were too shy. It is a very good snow angel.

events.text: The kiln opening. You are six, and the whole street has come to see the potter crack the kiln door after three days of fire. The heat comes out in a wall. Inside, row on row, the bowls are a blue nobody has ever made before.

choices.text: Ask the potter how the blue was made

effects.log: The potter tells you, all of it. You understand none of it, and remember every word.

choices.text: Reach for a bowl

effects.log: It is too hot. You drop it, and it does not break. The potter gives it to you.

events.text: This again. The street, the heat, the blue bowls. You are six, and you know that the bowl at the back on the left has a crack nobody will find until a wedding, years from now.

choices.text: Ask the potter how the blue was made

effects.log: The potter tells you, all of it. You understand none of it, and remember every word.

choices.text: Point out the cracked bowl

effects.log: The potter turns it in the light and finds the crack and looks at you very strangely. "Who taught you to see?"

choices.text: Help the potter carry the bowls

effects.log: You carry them all, two at a time, very carefully. Lives ago you only watched.

events.text: The bell day. You are six, and every bell of the town rings at once for a reason nobody tells you, and pigeons go up from every roof like a single grey cloud. An old man on the corner starts to cry, and smiles, and keeps crying.

choices.text: Count the bells

effects.log: You count forty-one bells before you lose track. You never find out what they were for.

choices.text: Chase the pigeons

effects.log: You chase them down three streets and come home late and happy.

events.text: This again. The bells, the pigeons, the old man on the corner crying and smiling. You are six, and you know the bells are for him: today is the day his lost son comes home.

choices.text: Count the bells

effects.log: You count forty-one bells before you lose track. You never find out what they were for.

choices.text: Go and stand with the old man

effects.log: You stand with him until his son comes round the corner. He holds your hand the whole time without noticing.

choices.text: Run to meet the son at the gate

effects.log: You meet the son at the town gate and bring him the short way. Lives ago he came the long way, and the old man waited an hour more.

events.text: A letter in a hand you have known since childhood: "The high ford, at the first full moon of autumn. No crowd. One of us should finally know." {npc} is waiting on the stones of the ford when you come, with the river loud on both sides.

choices.text: Step out onto the stones

mem.note: beat me at the high ford, and let me live

ok.log: Two hundred exchanges over the white water. When {npc} goes down on one knee in the shallows, you lower your hands. {He} laughs, and for once {he} sounds happy. "So that is what it takes."

fail.deathCause: your rival {npc}, at the high ford
fail.log: {npc} wins. {He} stands over you in the shallows a long moment, then hauls you out of the river. "Not like this," {he} says.

choices.text: Burn the letter

effects.log: {npc} waits on the ford for three nights. Then {he} goes home, and never speaks your name again.

events.text: {npc} has grown old beside you in this small world, always a step ahead or a step behind. Tonight {he} is at your gate with two practice staves and a lantern. "Before our knees go," {he} says. "In the yard. Properly, this time."

choices.text: Take a staff

mem.note: beat me in the yard by lantern light, at last

ok.log: It takes until the lantern gutters. When {npc} sits down in the dust, laughing, it is over, and somehow you are both glad.

fail.deathCause: your rival {npc}, in the yard by lantern light
fail.log: {npc} wins, as {he} so often did. {He} helps you up and says nothing for once, which is a kindness.

choices.text: Pour two cups instead

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} sets the staves down and drinks. You talk until morning. Neither of you won, and neither minds.

events.text: In the third hour of a night on the cloud sea the five energies of your body, which never answered anything, move together for the first time. The clouds around your isle turn slowly, as if stirred. A root is coming. You can choose what it becomes.

choices.text: Let it be wood, like the cloud pines

effects.log: It is wood, and it grows the way the cloud pines grow: out of nothing, on nothing.

choices.text: Let it be water, patient as the clouds

effects.log: It is water, deep and slow. It fills every empty place in you.

choices.text: Let it be metal, the edge of the white stairs

effects.log: It is metal, and it rings. You feel it sharpen.

events.text: A storm of the Heavenly Calendar passes over your isle, and for once you do not take shelter. Lightning walks the rock around you. The five energies of a body with no root gather in the centre of you, waiting for a word.

choices.text: Fire, the heat of the storm

effects.log: It is fire. It was always going to be fire.

choices.text: Earth, the rock you stand on

effects.log: It is earth, and nothing in heaven moves it.

choices.text: Water, the rain after

effects.log: It is water. It comes like the rain after a storm: everywhere at once.

events.text: Your domain has no root in it, because you have none: its sky has always been the plain blue of nothing. Tonight the five energies of your body turn together, once, and the sky of your domain waits to see what colour it will be.

choices.text: Let it be wood: a green sky of growing things

effects.log: It is wood. Your domain greens from end to end by morning, and the prayers smell of spring.

choices.text: Let it be fire: a sky like a forge

effects.log: It is fire. The sky of your domain goes gold at the edges and stays that way.

choices.text: Let it be earth: a sky like a mountain

effects.log: It is earth. Your domain settles like a great beast lying down.

events.text: Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, comes to your domain unannounced and kneels in its dry soil. "A god with no root," she says. "I have never seen one. Shall I plant one?" She holds out her hand. In it are five seeds.

choices.text: Take the seed of water

effects.log: It is water. Saengmo smiles as it takes, and leaves without another word.

choices.text: Take the seed of metal

effects.log: It is metal. It takes root like a blade going into a sheath.

choices.text: Take the seed of wood

effects.log: It is wood. Saengmo laughs: "Of course."

events.text: A travelling teacher of {pw_people} comes through the town to test the children for a spiritual root, with a grey stone that glows under the right hands. It glows for the miller's daughter and the twins. Under your hand it stays grey. Someone laughs.

choices.text: Keep your hand on the stone until they stop laughing

effects.log: You keep your hand on the grey stone for an hour, until the laughing stops and the teacher has to ask you to let go. The teacher looks at you a long time.

choices.text: Ask the teacher what a rootless child can do

effects.log: "Train twice as hard for half as much," the teacher says, "and hope the sky gets bored of saying no." It is the most honest thing any grown-up has told you.

events.text: Thirty years of training with nothing to hold it, and tonight, sitting on the bank where your world's first ford was, all of it moves at once. The river goes still to listen. A root is coming. You can choose what it becomes.

choices.text: Let it be water, like the river

effects.log: It is water, deep and slow. It fills every empty place in you.

choices.text: Let it be earth, like the ford stones

effects.log: It is earth, and it holds. Nothing will push you off your feet again.

choices.text: Let it be fire, like the kilns

effects.log: It is fire, and it burns steady, like a good kiln.

events.text: The storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} gathers over your own world, and the people of your world come out to watch it. In its rain stands {rgs_name}, {rgs_rel}, as on the last day. The river towns below see the face too, and go quiet.

choices.text: Ask their forgiveness, in front of everyone

effects.log: You ask, out loud, with your world watching. {rgs_name} smiles. "Go on up," they say. "Be kinder up there."

choices.text: Tell them you did all you could

ok.log: You hold your answer like a staff, and the shape breaks against it. The rain thins.

fail.log: Your voice cracks halfway. The shape looks at you sadly, and the storm takes the crack and widens it.

choices.text: Look away

effects.log: You look away. {rgs_name} nods, as if that is an answer too, and the clouds close behind them, darker.

events.arc: The Storm of Your World's Regrets

events.text: {rgs_name} is in the storm over the gate of {rgs_gate}: {rgs_rel}, as they were the moment your blow landed, in the world you made. "You made this world," they say, "and then you made me leave it. Tell me why."

choices.text: Ask their forgiveness

effects.log: You tell them the truth, all of it, and ask. They think for a long while. "Go on up," they say at last. "Carry it carefully."

choices.text: Answer that it had to be

ok.log: You hold your answer, and the shape breaks against it. You are not sure you won anything.

fail.log: Your answer cracks. The shape smiles, sadly, and the storm takes the crack and widens it.

choices.text: Refuse to answer

effects.log: You say nothing. They nod, as if that is an answer too, and the clouds close behind them, darker.

events.arc: The Storm of Your World's Regrets

events.text: The storm gathers over the gate of {rgs_gate}, and it is only a storm: cloud, wind, rain on the roofs of a world you love. The children of the river towns run out to splash in it. Nobody in it is angry with you.

choices.text: Give thanks for a clean heart

effects.log: You give thanks to your own small sky. It seems almost to nod.

choices.text: Splash with the children

effects.log: You go out and splash in it with them. It is only weather, and weather is good.

events.arc: The Storm of Your World's Regrets

events.text: The faces are gone, and the storm over the gate of {rgs_gate} is lighter for every one you answered. Down in the river towns someone has lit lanterns for you, a whole street of them, and they are not going out in the rain.

choices.text: Gather yourself for the gate

effects.log: You breathe, and gather, and look up. The gate is waiting, and the lanterns are still burning.

choices.text: Wave to the lanterns

effects.log: You wave. A whole street of lanterns waves back.

events.arc: The Storm of Your World's Regrets

events.text: A healer of {pw_people}, passing through, holds your wrist for a long time. "A Ghost Yin body," the healer says at last, very quietly, "in a yang-born child. My teacher's teacher wrote of it once. That child did not see thirty."

choices.text: Ask where the cure is found

ok.log: "Noon fire lives in the beasts of the hot hills, and in the sun-charms of the old kiln-priests," the healer says. "The deepest cold sleeps in caves and old barrows."

fail.log: The healer shakes their head. "Grow up first," they say. "Ask me again."

choices.text: Ask how long there is

effects.log: "Twenty-five years, if the sky is mean. Thirty, if it is kind." The healer does not soften it, and you are grateful later.

choices.text: Say you will live anyway

effects.log: The healer laughs and ruffles your hair. "Then live fast, and look hard."

events.text: The cold in your chest is a winter deeper. In an inn of the hot hills you hear of a Cinder Ram whose horns smoke at noon, and of an old kiln-priest in the same valley who still writes sun-charms on fired clay.

choices.text: Hunt the Cinder Ram

ok.log: It comes down the slope at noon like a grass fire. When it is over you take one ember-red horn tip, and for the first time in years your hands are warm.

fail.log: The ram leaves you in the scrub with a burn on your arm and nothing else. Next year, then.

choices.text: Buy a sun-charm from the kiln-priest (300 taels)

effects.log: The priest fires it at noon on the kiln roof. The clay tile is warm as bread when it is pressed into your hands.

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: You leave the hills with the cold sitting a little higher. Next year, you tell yourself. There is still a next year.

events.text: A shepherd tells you of a cave past the third ridge where the water at the bottom never freezes and never warms, and of a pale stone that lies in it. Another story tells of an old barrow by the fords, sealed with clay, where the first people of your world buried a jar of winter.

choices.text: Dive for the stone

ok.log: Down in the black water, past the last of the light. Your body does not feel the cold the way another would. Your hand closes on something colder than the pool.

fail.log: The cold drives you up before the bottom. You lie on the rock shaking for an hour.

choices.text: Open the barrow's clay seal

ok.log: The seal is a riddle more than a lock. On the third night you see it. Inside the jar is a frost that does not melt, and that is enough.

fail.log: The seal will not give. You leave it, and the barrow, for another year.

choices.text: Leave it for another year

effects.log: You turn back at the second ridge. The way down is warm in the sun and you cannot feel it at all.

events.text: The fire half and the cold half lie side by side on your table, and the air above them shimmers like a road in summer. The healer's old book is open at the page for the Returning Pill. It is a short page.

choices.text: Brew it yourself

ok.log: Nine days at the stove, turning the fire up for the yang and down for the yin. On the ninth night the pot goes quiet, and in it is one pill, half black, half white.

fail.log: The pot cracks on the sixth day. The halves are safe, the pot is not. You will try again.

choices.text: Pay the healer to brew it (500 taels)

effects.log: The healer takes a month. A small clay box comes to your door, and in it is one pill, half black, half white.

choices.text: Wait until your hands are steadier

effects.log: You wrap the two halves in cloth and put them away. The cold does not wait with you.

events.text: The pill is half black and half white, warm on one side and cold on the other. When it goes down, the cold in your chest stops climbing for the first time in your life. In the night it begins to turn, slowly, and you understand you can let it choose its own shape.

choices.text: Let the turning remake the body

effects.log: You let go, and the yin and the yang in you begin to chase each other like the two fish of the old diagram.

choices.text: Follow the dream to the cave

effects.log: You follow the cold down into the dark of the dream, to a flat stone by your world's first river, and the words cut into its underside.

events.text: In a domain whose god faded long ago, a bronze censer stands on a broken altar, and smoke still rises from it: the smoke of the first prayer ever made to that god, still burning after all this time.

choices.text: Take the censer, and carry the prayer on

effects.log: You carry it home with both hands. The old smoke curls round you when you train, and the qi follows it.

choices.text: Leave it burning where it is

effects.log: You leave it. Some prayers belong where they were made.

events.text: Under the floor of the Hall of Heaven's Register, where a flagstone has cracked, lies a seal of black jade: the seal a domain was first written with. It is warm, and it grows warmer when you hold it.

choices.text: Ask the Registrar whose it is

ok.log: "Nobody's now," says the Registrar, who has been looking for it for an age. "Keep it. It likes you."

fail.log: The Registrar takes it back under the floor, with thanks, and a look you do not like.

choices.text: Put it back under the stone

effects.log: You put it back. The flagstone mends itself overnight.

events.text: In the attic of the oldest house in the river towns, behind a chest of mouldering nets, a clay lantern is burning. The family swears nobody has lit it in living memory. It is the lantern of the night {pw_kingdom} lit its first town.

choices.text: Buy it from the family (40 taels)

effects.log: They are glad to see it go; it frightens the children. It burns beside your bed from then on, and the years go slower.

choices.text: Leave it where it has always been

effects.log: You leave it. The family looks relieved, and a little sorry.

events.text: At the first ford of your world, the stones the first people stepped on are still there under the water. One of them, smooth as an egg, will not move when the river floods. The ferry folk say it does not like to be moved.

choices.text: Lift it anyway

ok.log: It comes up out of the river like something waking. It is heavy, and then it is not. You carry it home and your hands are stronger for it.

fail.log: It will not come. The river laughs at you all afternoon.

choices.text: Leave it in the ford

effects.log: You leave it. The ferry folk nod at you in a new way after that.
